decisions.reason: As an organic extension of a core ham line, it fits the firm's stated organic expansion and a large incumbent with some slack would likely keep it unless results clearly fall short of aspiration levels.

This organic Kasseler variant stays close to established capabilities and customers, so in a growing industry management would usually retain it while learning about demand rather than search for alternatives immediately.
Organic pepper salami is still a familiar salami-line extension that supports the organic range, making continued market presence more likely than withdrawal absent clear underperformance.

The beef-in-teriyaki-aspic item is a narrower and more experimental deli-counter specialty, so if its uptake is below aspiration it is the most plausible product to prune and reallocate resources from.
Fennel-flavoured sliced salami is closer to the core than D but remains a taste-specific niche variant, which makes it vulnerable if retailer acceptance and repeat demand do not meet aspirations.
Liver pâté with veal fits the firm's traditional premium meat-specialty competence, so organisational slack and product familiarity make retention somewhat more likely than withdrawal.
